body:
> maybe it is possible for an autocommand to set buf->b_ffname or buf->b_sfname

:+1: That's where I got stuck. I checked to see if we were doing things correctly in `terminal_open` and friends, and didn't find any problems. 

It might not be a bad idea to wrap all access to `buf->b_ffname`/`buf->b_sfname` in setters like `buf_set_ffname` which then abort if a NULL is passed, or do something sensible.

Tried a few silly autocommands but cannot replicate. 

> It might not be a bad idea to wrap all access to buf->b_ffname/buf->b_sfname in setters like buf_set_ffname which then abort if a NULL is passed, or do something sensible.

Alternatives: Either set those vars to be an empty string instead of NULL, or do something to `os_stat()` to allow a NULL path. Problem with the first choice is those values are checked for NULL in a bunch of different places too.

> Alternatives: Either set those vars to be an empty string instead of NULL, or do something to os_stat() to allow a NULL path.

I don't like either of those options, because whatever is setting the thing to NULL has a bug, then we're just covering it up. aborting at least fails earlier in the codepath, so we might get closer to the actual issue.

I just discovered something kind of interesting. If I open neovim via directory (e.g. `nvim .`), NERDTree comes up. If I select a file then `:w` then I hit the assertion. If I open the same file directly (`nvim foo.bar`) and `:w` everything works just fine. This led me to believe that NERDTree may be causing the issue, so I opened a file, selected a different file with NERDTree, `:w`, crash.

_edit_: ah, never mind... seem as though opening _any_ other file/buffer causes a crash. Even just typing `:e baz.bar`. My mistake.

I just experienced this as well during a simple :w -- unfortunately no core dump.

Since then, if I am working with the files that had swaps, I can open the file, and recover the swap file. But when I try to :w nvim simply hangs. Ctrl-C breaks out of it, and leaves me with an empty buffer.

Deleting the swap file makes the problem go away.

@benfleis If you're on macOS a backtrace should have [automatically logged](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/wiki/Development-tips#backtrace-macos--osx). 

If you're on linux, a backtrace from the hang would be useful. When it hangs after `:w`, attach to the hung `nvim` process with gdb. Then get the backtrace via the gdb command `thread apply all bt full`. Use the `tee` trick [here](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/wiki/Development-tips#backtrace-linux) to save the log to a file.
AFAIK there's no need to enable core files for the Console auto-logging feature.
I meant that if cores had been enabled, I could have simply used that to get a backtrace, and even shared the corefile itself.

Getting this crash with development release v0.2.0-1162-gbc6d868 on Ubuntu 16.04

Not sure if it is related, but I'm using [vim-go](https://github.com/fatih/vim-go) which reformats the code and updates the buffer on save.

Output of gdb bt full on the coredump:

[backtrace_full.txt](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/files/893193/backtrace_full.txt)

For me this occurs when I have the following auto command enabled and open a file in a parent folder (e.g. nvim README.md doesn't crash but nvim ../README.md does).
```
  au BufWritePre * :silent! Neomake " Includes auto tidy for html etc
```
